column1: # clues.tsv for ft_is_prime — pedagogic hints only. NEVER state the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><member CASE label><TAB>...   (fires if ANY member case fails)
# Lines are shown most-fundamental first; the first line doubles as the "foothold".
Where does the very definition of a prime start? Below which integer can a number never qualify, and which two small numbers are the first that do? What does your function answer for each of them?
4 is not prime. Which numbers divide it, and does your function ever find one of them? Try the squares of other small primes too: 9, 25, 49.

Every answer here is 0 or 1. For very large inputs, does anything your code computes on the way to it grow past what its type holds on some platform? (What C promises about the width of each type: docs/testing.md, under ilp32.)
